newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude weak, support at $20.90,$20.5.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude weak, support at $20.90,$20.5.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

+ June crude expected to register further losses on Wednesday, although some chartists mildly bullish if holds $20.55. + Gasoline also fragile. Support around 63.50/10 gap. + Heating oil also under pressure with gap support at 54.85/95 on June chart, and bottom of spot chart gap at 55.40/57.50.
NYMEX crude futures were expected to fall on Wednesday as bearish oil stock fundamentals crushed the bullish technical patterns of the past few days, chartists said.
NYMEX June crude ended one cent lower at $21.38 a barrel on Tuesday, while gasoline closed 0.29 cent higher at 64.76 cents a gallon and heating oil 0.17 cent lower at 56.48 cents a gallon.

Some chartists had thought June crude's break above trendline resistance on Monday would pave the wave for further gains after some consolidation, but bearish American Petroleum Inistitute data released late on Tuesday has cut the uptrend dead.
"I thought the break of $20.55 had cleared the way for higher prices," said a Washington-based chartist.
She said the contract's action with regard to $20.55 was crucial. "If it holds we could be in for another rally further down the line."
She said the upside gap on the pit trade only chart spanning $18.72/55 would be a key support area for the contract.
Victor Yu, a vice-president at Refco in New York, was expecting to further losses.
"Monday's rally was more the result of short-covering than first buying," he said.
Another factor in the bulls' disfavour was the fact the June contract had failed to hold above Fibonacci resistance at $21.50, Yu said.
He pegged key support for the June contract at $20.91 in line with trendline support. Below that, he saw support around $19.85.
Products were similarly fragile.

Looking at the pit trade-only chart, Charles Gray at Prudential Bache in London pegged support for front-month gasoline at 63.85, 63.40 and 62.80 cents. Below there he saw Fibonacci support at 62.50 cents.
"With a 6 cent move in 5 days, a 50 percent retracement is 62.50 cents," he said in his daily energy report.
On the heating oil front, chartists saw key support for the June contract around the upside gap spanning 54.85/95 cents seen between May 9 and 12.
Gray, meanwhile, focused on the 55.40/57.50 gap seen between April 30 and May 1.

"Heat managed to fill most of its existing gap to 57.50 cents, but like unleaded is now vulnerable to some profit-taking. Initial support is the bottom of the gap at 55.40 cents," he said. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714
